minutes.headline: Commissioners backed a pay-and-access deadline for a broken-meter customer, and set a base business rate for Zach's water hauling.
minutes.summary: The Lunenburg Water District commissioners spent most of the meeting on a White Street account with a zero-read meter and estimated bills, and on the superintendent's report. That report covered the Hickory Hills pilot study, the Mass DOT water main bid timing and a large cost increase, new DEP water restrictions, bulk water hauling rates, PFAS and ARPA funding. Employees were appointed and a commissioner was sworn in; reorganizing the board was put off until a full board is present.

public_comment.topic: Asked what the annual meeting cost the district, including police details and counsel.

votes.motion: Accept the articles of the March 25th annual meeting
Appoint employees for the next fiscal year

budget_items.what_was_said: Clerk described undercharges and overcharges from estimating a zero-read meter.
Commissioners questioned why the estimate rose so far from the original quote and wanted the engineer to explain.
Board settled the hauler on the base business rate rather than the highest block.
Police detail, counsel and employee overtime were discussed as extra costs.
Clerk is checking whether the district can apply for ARPA money through the town.

decisions.decision: Customer to be offered a payment based on 1500 cubic feet per quarter and a date to allow meter access, or the water is shut off.
Hauler to pay the base business rate; the minutes will cite the 720 per 100 cubic feet figure.
Board reorganization deferred until a full board is present.
Draft camera video policy to be reviewed and brought back at the next meeting.

what_happened.line: Commissioners agreed to offer the White Street customer a payment plan and a date for meter access, or the water is shut off.
The board settled the bulk water hauler on the base business rate rather than the highest block.
Employees were appointed for the next fiscal year and the March annual meeting articles were accepted; the vote counts were not audible.
Reorganizing the board was deferred until a full board is present.
Commissioners questioned why the water main estimate rose so far from the original quote and wanted the engineer to explain.

why_it_matters: Estimated bills from a zero-read meter can run over or under what was used, and the shutoff deadline shows how the district handles an account that blocks meter access.
The hauling rate and the water main cost increase bear on what water costs and on what ratepayers may later be asked to fund, though the minutes do not say how the main would be paid for.
